gaps.explanation: 'It's' is short for 'it is' or 'it has'; here it means 'it has been raining'. The possessive is 'its'.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

gaps.sentence: We ___ money by cycling to work instead of driving.
gaps.hint: to keep money instead of spending it
gaps.explanation: 'Save money by doing something' means to avoid spending it; 'earn' means to receive money for work.

gaps.sentence: ___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
gaps.explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

gaps.sentence: The money was divided ___ the four children.
gaps.hint: for a group of more than two
gaps.explanation: 'Among' is traditionally used for more than two; 'between' is preferred for exactly two.

gaps.sentence: The country is facing a serious ___ crisis.
gaps.hint: connected with money, trade and industry
gaps.explanation: 'Economic' means connected with the economy; 'economical' means saving money.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: She is ___ of hearing after years beside the speakers.
gaps.explanation: 'Hard of hearing' is the fixed phrase; 'hardly' is an adverb.
